reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is comparing individual performance across eras where league-wide success rates change systematically. The authors introduce a 'prowess' metric P_i(t) = x_i(t)/y_i(t) that normalizes raw counts x_i by opportunities y_i. To remove the confounding effect of league-wide trend, they define a renormalized metric x^D_i(t) = x_i(t)/⟨P(t)⟩, where ⟨P(t)⟩ is the league-average prowess. This division stabilizes the variance and restores stationarity, enabling valid cross-era comparisons. The method relies on the assumption that all time-dependent factors affecting individual performance are captured by the league average. Failure occurs when this assumption breaks, e.g., due to specialization or rule changes affecting only subsets of players.
